scenes.heading: Pricing your writing: per word, per hour, or per project

sents.d: Pricing your writing: per word, per hour, or per project
Each model suits different types of writing work.
Per-word pricing is common for content writing and journalism, is easy for clients to understand, but penalizes concise writing and rewards padding — a poor incentive when clarity is the actual goal.
Hourly pricing works better for research-heavy or highly custom work where word count doesn't reflect effort, but requires trust since clients can't predict the final cost as easily.

Project-based pricing (a flat fee for a defined piece — a landing page, an email sequence, a blog post) gives clients cost certainty and rewards efficiency, and tends to be the norm for copywriting specifically, as opposed to long-form content writing which is often priced per word.

take: Choose a pricing model that rewards clarity and efficiency.
